## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Esoteric ritual manual translated by **Ajitasena** ([阿質達霰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%BF%E8%B3%AA%E9%81%94%E9%9C%B0)) at Ānxī during the Kāiyuán reign — the first of two short Ucchuṣma manuals that complement his three-fascicle scripture [KR6j0455](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0455) (T1227). The deity here is named in his **Huìjī jīngāng** 穢跡金剛 ("Filth-Tracks Vajra") aspect, the form of Ucchuṣma especially associated with the consumption of impurity. Sanskrit affiliation in canwww: *Vajragarbharatnarājatantra(sūtra)*. Korean Tripiṭaka K1265; Nanjio 0966.

**Abstract**

The text is structured as a ritual catalogue rather than as a continuous scripture: the deity, his *bīja* and *mantra*, then a series of applied dhāraṇī-rites (法術 *fǎshù*, "method-techniques") for various practical ends — illness-healing, hostile-spirit expulsion, protection of person and dwelling, snake- and venom-cure, food-purification. The framing is *huìjī* / Ucchuṣma's own self-exposition: "I, Ucchuṣma-Vajra, now expound this dhāraṇī-method…". This format — the deity speaking his own ritual programme — is characteristic of late Indian *kriyā-tantra* and its Sinitic reception. Together with [KR6j0457](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0457) (T1229), the text was the foundational scripture for the East-Asian **Ucchuṣma-Vajra** cult, which became important especially in **Chán** (Zen) monasticism for purification of latrines and for emergency demon-subduing rites.

The dating bracket follows Ajitasena's Kāiyuán-era activity at Ānxī (713–741).
